A good article gives its reader room to think. That starts with the words, but it also depends on the space around them: the length of a line, the pace between paragraphs, and where an image enters the story.

## A steady rhythm

The headline introduces the idea. The summary offers a way in. The body then settles into a comfortable measure, with enough space between lines to make the next sentence easy to find.

> The aim is to make the story easy to follow, from the first sentence to the last.

Images need the same care. A subject that works in a wide article may disappear in a small preview. Editorial framing lets the placement change while keeping the subject visible.

![The same scene, with a more generous preferred frame.](./scene.png)

## Content that travels

The website can offer the richest experience, while a feed carries the complete article into a reader's own tools. Both start with the same text and images.
